Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

murder noun

also murderer, killing, homicide, commit murder, a murder mystery, murderess, parricide, murder (verb)

classical

Cic. Mil. 12 (Lewis & Short)
Sall. Jug. 31.13: caedem in aliquem facere
Traupman 196: murder by striking

caedēs, caedis f.

noun, third declension

murder, killing; slaughter

The usual classical word for a killing, of one person or many: murder, massacre, slaughter in battle. To commit murder is caedem facere (Sall. Jug. 31.13) or committere (Quint.); to murder someone, occīdere or interficere (see kill).

Other words

  • nex, necis f. — a violent death, murder

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 10 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 349; Traupman 196

    Death by violence, seen from the victim’s side; outside fixed phrases (vītae necisque potestās, power of life and death, Caesar) mostly in poetry. Traupman gives it for murder.

  • homicīdium, homicīdiī n. — homicide, murder (as a charge)

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Quint. 3.10.1: sī quis homicīdiī accūsētur (Lewis & Short); Tac. G. 21; Traupman 195; Traupman 329

    The term of the courts from Quintilian on; Cicero says caedēs and, of the charge, inter sīcāriōs.

  • homicīda, homicīdae m./f. — a murderer, a murderess

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.30 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 196

    Cicero sets it beside sīcārius, an assassin who uses a dagger, and parricīda, the murderer of a parent or kinsman (Phil. 2.30–31).

  • sīcārius, sīcāriī m. — an assassin, a murderer

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 8 (Lewis & Short); Quint. 10.1.12

    From sīca, a dagger, but used of any murderer (Quint. 10.1.12). Inter sīcāriōs accūsāre, dēfendere: on a charge of murder (Cic. Rosc. Am. 90).

  • occīsiō, occīsiōnis f. — a killing, a murder

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 41: sī caedēs et occīsiō facta nōn erit (Lewis & Short: “class. but rare”); Traupman 196

  • parricīda, parricīdae m./f. — the murderer of a parent or near relative

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. parricīda; Traupman 196

  • necātor, necātōris m. — a murderer

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Macr. S. 1.12.9 (Lewis & Short: post-classical); Traupman 196

  • necātrīx, necātrīcis f. — a murderess

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Aug. Cons. Evang. (Lewis & Short: late Latin); Traupman 196

    Late; a murderess is classically homicīda, which is of either gender.

Examples

  • In hōc librō dē caede quaeritur.

    This book is a murder mystery.composed

  • necāre

    to murder (by cruel means)Traupman 196

  • trucīdāre

    to murder (violently, ruthlessly)Traupman 196

  • caedere

    to murder (by striking)Traupman 196
